pictures.scene: Maes, An Old Woman Praying — an old woman in a black gown and a white linen cap sits close to the table in the dark of her room with her two knotted hands pressed together and her lined face lifted into the light, her eyes open and looking away past us as she speaks, the open book, the spectacles and the quill lying untouched on the red cloth in front of her, then jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart, in a certain town there was a judge who neither feared god nor respected men, …
pictures.name: pd_maes_an_old_woman_praying

pictures.scene: Israels, The Widow — a widow in a heavy dark gown and a grey headcloth comes barefoot up the sand from the sea with her head bowed and her mouth set, a small girl gripping one of her hands and a smaller child clinging to the other, the long pale streaked light of the evening lying over the breakers behind the three of them, and there was a widow in that town who kept appealing to him, give me justice against my adversary, for a while he refused, but later he said to himself, though i neither fear god nor respect men, …
pictures.name: pd_israels_weduwe

pictures.scene: Brueghel the Younger, The Tax Collector's Office — a crowded office packed to the ceiling with hanging money bags and bundled papers, where a press of countrymen in blue and red jerkins shoulder each other forward with their hats pulled off and held against their chests, one holding out a folded paper, one carrying a dead goose, an old woman at the left bent under her basket, every face turned toward the desk and waiting to be dealt with, yet because this widow keeps pestering me, i will give her justice, then she will stop wearing me out with her perpetual requests, and the lord said, listen to the words of the unjust judge, …
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_tax_collectors_office

pictures.scene: King David Kneeling Before an Altar — the crowned king kneels in polished armour under a great gold cope worked all over with little painted scenes, one bare knee down on the step, his hand laid flat on his breast and his bearded face turned up and sideways into the light with his lips parted, his harp leaning against him at the right and an angel sweeping down out of the cloud above his shoulder, will not god bring about justice for his elect who cry out to him day and night, will he continue to defer their help, i tell you, he will promptly carry out justice on their behalf, nevertheless, when the son of man comes, will he find faith on earth, …
pictures.name: pd_king_david_kneeling_before_an_altar

pictures.scene: Gottlieb, Jews Praying in the Synagogue on Yom Kippur — the house of prayer is packed from the front bench to the gallery rail, men in white striped prayer shawls standing close together with their eyes shut and their heads leaned on their hands, one of them holding the covered scroll against his chest, a boy at the left looking straight out, the women crowded along the gallery above under the grey stone arches, to some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, he also told this parable, two men went up to the temple to pray, one was a pharisee and the other a tax collector, …
pictures.name: pd_gottlieb_jews_praying_on_yom_kippur

pictures.scene: Van der Valckert, Regents of the Shopkeepers Guild — two men in black with tall stiff hats and wide starched ruffs sit at the carpet-covered table and look straight out at us, one with his fingers spread flat on the written sheet in front of him, the other holding down the ledger with the quill standing in the inkpot, the guild's brass balance hanging on its chain between their heads with both pans empty, the pharisee stood by himself and prayed, god, i thank you that i am not like the other men, swindlers, evildoers, adulterers, or even like this tax collector, i fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that i acquire, …
pictures.name: pd_valckert_regents_kramergild

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, An Elderly Man in Prayer — an old man in a plain brown coat stands alone in the dark with his two rough hands pressed palm to palm in front of his chest, his grey head bowed and his eyes closed so that the light falls only on his forehead, his beard and his knuckles, the open book lying forgotten on the table below his elbows, but the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven, instead, he beat his breast and said, god, have mercy on me, a sinner, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_elderly_man_in_prayer

pictures.scene: Neuhuys, Mother and Child — a young mother in a white cap and a long dark working dress sits on a rush chair in the half-light of her cottage with the baby held up on her knee, her hand under one small bare foot and the child's fist closed round a little spoon, her head bent and her eyes down on him, the mending basket standing on the table at the left, i tell you, this man, rather than the pharisee, went home justified, for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted, now people were even bringing their babies to jesus for him to place his hands on them, and when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them, …
pictures.name: pd_neuhuys_moeder_en_kind

pictures.scene: De Wet, Christ Blessing the Children — Christ sits low on the stone step in a pale robe with a faint ring of gold about His head, His hand on His breast and His face bent down toward the smallest of them, and on every side the mothers press their children forward, one in a blue skirt kneeling with a baby under her arm, a little girl in yellow kneeling at His knee with her hands together, a boy in a red cap sitting on the pavement in front, the dark doorway of the house standing open behind them, but jesus called the children to him and said, let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of god belongs to such as these, truly i tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of god like a little child will never enter it, …
pictures.name: pd_dewet_christus_zegent_kinderen

pictures.scene: Hofmann, Christ and the Rich Young Ruler — Christ stands against the grey stone wall in a red tunic and a dark blue cloak with His head turned toward the young man beside Him and one open hand stretched away out of the picture, and the young ruler, dressed in a jewelled turban and a heavy cream mantle over green silk, stands close in at the right with his face lowered and his hands folded in front of him, listening and not yet answering, then a certain ruler asked him, good teacher, what must i do to inherit eternal life, why do you call me good, jesus replied, no one is good except god alone, …
pictures.name: pd_hofmann_christ_and_the_rich_young_ruler

pictures.scene: Philippe de Champaigne, Moses with the Ten Commandments — Moses stands out of the black in a blue robe and a gold-embroidered mantle with the two horns of light in his white hair, holding up the grey tablet against his shoulder so that the numbered commandments run down it line by line in front of him, his other hand resting on the ledge with the gilded rod across it, his face turned to us and his eyes wide open, you know the commandments, do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother, all these i have kept from my youth, he said, …
pictures.name: pd_champaigne_moses_with_the_ten_commandments

pictures.scene: Master of Alkmaar, The Seven Works of Mercy, Feeding the Hungry — in a pale brick street a young woman in a white apron carries a basket of round loaves out of her doorway, a man in a long blue gown takes them and passes them on, and the poor of the town close in on him from the right, a woman in green holding out her hand, a little child reaching up from below, a crippled man dragging himself forward on his blocks in the foreground, Christ standing quietly among the crowd behind them, on hearing this, jesus told him, you still lack one thing, sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven, then come, follow me, but when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy, …
pictures.name: pd_alkmaar_barmhartigheid

pictures.scene: Tissot, The Caravan — a long train of loaded camels comes winding down the bare tan hillside and out toward us along the narrow track, the nearest beast hung all over with red and blue tasselled trappings and a striped awning spread above its hump, a rider wrapped to the eyes in white sitting high on the camel beside it, and behind them the line of travellers runs back up the slope until it is only flecks of red and white on the empty hill, seeing the man's sadness, jesus said, how hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of god, indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of god, …
pictures.name: pd_tissot_caravan

pictures.scene: Elijah Taken Up in a Chariot of Fire — the old prophet is carried straight up off the ground, his white mantle filling half the picture as it drags out behind him and one bare foot still hanging below the hem, his bearded face turned back and up over his shoulder, the flame running out under him in long pale tongues and the gold rim of the chariot wheel turning at the right, the dark shore and the water lying far down at the bottom of the picture, those who heard this asked, who then can be saved, but jesus said, what is impossible with man is possible with god, …
pictures.name: pd_angeli_elijah_taken_up_in_a_chariot_of_fire

pictures.scene: Homer, The Herring Net — a fisherman in oilskins and a sou'wester stands bent far over the side of the dory in the open sea, hauling the dripping net up over the gunwale with both hands while the caught herring hang silver and blue all along the mesh, the green swell running under the boat and a red float riding the water in front of him, the grey weather lying flat and empty above, look, said peter, we have left all we had to follow you, truly i tell you, jesus replied, no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of god, …
pictures.name: pd_homer_the_herring_net

pictures.scene: Bauernfeind, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — the whole pale city lies across the picture in the early light, the long sand-coloured wall running the width of it and the domes and towers packed close behind, the olive trees and stony terraces falling away in front, and down at the bottom a little company of travellers with staffs and bundles comes along the hill road toward the gate, one woman carrying a basket on her head, will fail to receive many times more in this age, and in the age to come, eternal life, then jesus took the twelve aside and said to them, look, we are going up to jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the son of man will be fulfilled, …
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_jerusalem_from_the_mount_of_olives

pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Carrying the Cross — Christ stands against a stormy blue-green ground in a deep blue mantle over a red robe, the crown of thorns pressed down on His head with thin lines of blood running from it into His beard, His eyes lifted and brimming, and both of His long pale hands laid round the beam of the yellow cross, holding it rather than struggling under it, he will be delivered over to the gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon, they will flog him and kill him, and on the third day he will rise again, …
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_christ_carrying_the_cross

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Beggars — three crippled men in white tabards and foxtails wait on the grass beside a brick wall, one leaning forward on his crutch with his mouth open and his face turned up toward whoever is passing, another sitting flat on the ground with his stumps strapped into leather pads and a stick braced in each hand, and behind them a woman in a black hood walks away carrying the alms bowl, but the disciples did not understand any of these things, the meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what he was saying, as jesus drew near to jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_beggars

pictures.scene: Repin, Religious Procession in Kursk Province — an enormous crowd comes down a dusty road under the gold icon banners, villagers and merchants and women in bonnets packed shoulder to shoulder behind a priest in a stiff gold brocade vestment, while out in front of them all a lame boy in a grey coat throws himself forward on his crutch with his face lifted and his free arm flung out, and a mounted officer blocks the road at the left, when he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening, jesus of nazareth is passing by, they told him, …
pictures.name: pd_repin_religious_procession_in_kursk_province

pictures.scene: Breu, The Crowd Shouts Against Him — a bishop in a jewelled white mitre and a pale gold cope stands on the step with one finger lifted to quiet the man in front of him, a grey-haired official in a scarlet gown and a black cap who leans up toward him with a rolled paper in his fist and his mouth wide open, and behind the two of them a press of men in red and green hats shouts over their heads with their arms thrown up in the air, so he called out, jesus, son of david, have mercy on me, those who led the way admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, son of david, have mercy on me, …
pictures.name: pd_breu_de_menigte_roept_tegen_hem

pictures.scene: Poussin, Christ and the Woman Taken in Adultery — Christ stands barefoot in a blue robe and a heavy red cloak in the middle of a paved square under the stone town, turning His head toward the man kneeling at His right and reaching both hands out low to beckon him, one finger pointing down at the stones in front of Him while the kneeling man spreads his empty hands open toward Him and a woman sits bowed on the pavement at the left, jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to him, when he had been brought near, jesus asked him, what do you want me to do for you, lord, he said, let me see again, …
pictures.name: pd_poussin_christ_and_the_woman_taken_in_adultery

pictures.scene: Ancher, Sunshine in the Blind Woman's Room — an old blind woman in a black hood and a blue-green sleeved dress stands at the end of the scrubbed plank table in a bare cottage room, her clouded eyes half shut and her face lifted a little toward the warmth, one hand laid flat on the table and the other hanging at her side, while the low sun prints two burning squares of the window across the wall beside her and sets the jars and fruit on the sill alight, receive your sight, jesus replied, your faith has healed you, immediately he received his sight and followed jesus, glorifying god, and all the people who saw this gave praise to god, …
pictures.name: pd_ancher_solskin_i_den_blindes_stue

lines.text: Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart:
In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected men.
And there was a widow in that town who kept appealing to him, Give me justice against my adversary.
For a while he refused, but later he said to himself, Though I neither fear God nor respect men,
yet because this widow keeps pestering me, I will give her justice. Then she will stop wearing me out with her perpetual requests.
And the Lord said, Listen to the words of the unjust judge.
Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night? Will He continue to defer their help?
I tell you, He will promptly carry out justice on their behalf. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?
To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable:
Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, God, I thank You that I am not like the other men, swindlers, evildoers, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.
But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven.
Instead, he beat his breast and said, God, have mercy on me, a sinner!
I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.
Now people were even bringing their babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. And when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them.
But Jesus called the children to Him and said, Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.
Then a certain ruler asked Him, Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?
Why do you call Me good? Jesus replied. No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.
All these I have kept from my youth, he said.
On hearing this, Jesus told him, You still lack one thing: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.
But when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.
Seeing the man's sadness, Jesus said, How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!
Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
Those who heard this asked, Who then can be saved?
But Jesus said, What is impossible with man is possible with God.
Look, said Peter, we have left all we had to follow You.
Truly I tell you, Jesus replied, no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
will fail to receive many times more in this age, and in the age to come, eternal life.
Then Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
He will be delivered over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon.
They will flog Him and kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again.
But the disciples did not understand any of these things. The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what He was saying.
As Jesus drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
Jesus of Nazareth is passing by, they told him.
So he called out, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!
Those who led the way admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, Son of David, have mercy on me!
Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him. When he had been brought near, Jesus asked him,
What do you want Me to do for you? Lord, he said, let me see again.
Receive your sight! Jesus replied. Your faith has healed you.
Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus, glorifying God. And all the people who saw this gave praise to God.
